item.title: Christian Gonzalez, Patriots agree to four-year extension
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Gonzalez has agreed to a deal that will make him the league's highest-paid corner, ending a contract dispute.
item.content:encoded:
The two sides cut it close, but in the end, they've gotten it done.

According to multiple reports, the Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez have agreed to a four-year contract extension.

The deal is reportedly worth $135 million with $102 million guaranteed, which makes Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in league history.

Gonzalez, the No. 17 overall pick of the 2023 draft, had been seeking a new deal throughout the offseason. There was some question as to whether or not Gonzalez would play in New England’s season opener against Seattle on Wednesday night.

Now that the contract is settled, Gonzalez has every reason to be on the field.

Gonzalez, 24, was a second-team AP All-Pro in 2024 and a Pro Bowler in 2025. He had 10 passes defensed in 14 regular-season games last year. He also had seven passes defensed, a forced fumble, and an interception in New England’s four 2025 postseason games.

New England and Seattle will kick off the 2026 season on Wednesday night at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer: We have "great confidence" in T.J. Bass replacing Tyler Smith
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys showed how much they valued T.J.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys showed how much they valued T.J. Bass as a reserve offensive lineman by using a second-round restricted free agent tender to hold onto him this offseason and Bass will get an immediate chance to show the wisdom of that decision.

Bass will step in as the team's left guard while Tyler Smith is out of action due to thumb surgery. Smith is expected to miss 4-6 weeks as a result of the procedure and head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on Monday that the team is not expecting a major drop in play with Bass in the lineup.

"Tyler Smith's a great player, but we feel really confident in T.J., and he's put great film on here," Schottenheimer said, via the team's website. "He's played next to Cooper Beebe, he's played next to [Tyler] Guyton, so that's nothing new, the communication and all that stuff. . . . We tendered him the way we tendered him because we trust this guy as a football player. He's a damn good football player that unfortunately is just playing behind a lot of really, really good players. So we have great confidence in T.J."

Bass has started 10 games over the last three seasons and he'll have a chance to show he's ready for a full-time role in the starting lineup for Dallas or someone else in the coming weeks.

item.title: C.J. Stroud: Pressure is a privilege
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Texans have gone to the playoffs in each of quarterback C.J.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans have gone to the playoffs in each of quarterback C.J. Stroud's three NFL seasons and they've won a game in each of those trips, but that hasn't cemented Stroud as the franchise quarterback in Houston.

Stroud has not been able to match his rookie production in either of the last two seasons and he threw five interceptions in last year's postseason. which helped keep a contract extension out of reach this offseason. The team doesn’t plan on talking about one once the season starts and that leaves Stroud in position to make his case for the kind of deal that would remove any doubt about his place in the team's future.

That cloud overhead could impact some players in a negative way, but Stroud said he's embracing the position he's in as the 2026 season gets underway.

"Pressure is a privilege," Stroud said, via DJ Bien-Amie of ESPN.com. "I'm excited. I've always been challenged in my career. I've always had to persevere through things, and I think this is something that I'm grateful for. I didn't wake up and forget how to play football."

The Texans are expected to have one of the best defenses in the league and that should impact how much the Texans ask Stroud to do on a weekly basis. If he can handle that charge while the Texans make another run to the playoffs, it is hard to imagine a deal won't come together in Houston and Stroud can begin making his case against the Ravens this weekend.

item.title: JC Latham gives opponents a warning about what the Titans' offensive line won't allow
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Titans offensive tackle JC Latham wants opposing teams to know they're not going to get away with any cheap shots on quarterback Cam Ward.
item.content:encoded:
Titans offensive tackle JC Latham wants opposing teams to know they're not going to get away with any cheap shots on quarterback Cam Ward.

Latham said a big part of the offensive line coming together this offseason has been agreeing that they need to play with more fight, which will include going after any opponent who goes after Ward.

"Culture is what you stand for and what you allow," Latham said. "This offseason we all did a moment of self-reflecting of, we want to be the offensive line that we know we can be. We can't be no pushovers, we can't be nobody's bitch, just being completely honest. So all the late hits, all the extra stuff that defenses do, if we want to be what we know we can be, we can't stand for that."

Latham said the Titans' new coaching staff has told the offensive linemen that they all have to have their teammates' backs.

"If any of us gets into it, we're all getting into it. We're all stepping up," he said. "You just can't go for no bullshit."

item.title: NFL fines Cam Taylor-Britt and four other players for preseason Week 3 infractions
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The NFL fines players for illegal hits during the preseason, but for the third and final week of the preseason, those fines were fairly limited.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL fines players for illegal hits during the preseason, but for the third and final week of the preseason, those fines were fairly limited.

The biggest fine went to Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt, who was fined $7,791 for unnecessary roughness. Ordinarily that money would be taken out of a player's Week 1 game check, but Taylor-Britt is already suspended without pay for Week 1 for a violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy, so his fine will come out of his Week 2 check.

Four other players were fined for preseason Week 3: Buffalo's Jalon Kilgore $5,560 for illegal use of the helmet, Minnesota's Jermar Jefferson $5,583 for facemasking, New Orleans' Danny Stutsman $7,011 for illegal use of the helmet, and Pittsburgh's Doneiko Slaughter $4,917 for taunting.

Only five fines for a week is unusually low in the NFL: In preseason Week 1, nine players were fined, and in preseason Week 2, 16 players were fined. It's likely that the NFL decided not to bother fining some players who were cut after the preseason finale, as those players won't be getting Week 1 game checks anyway. The five players who were fined all remain under contract and have paychecks the NFL can dock.

The NFL and NFL Players Association collectively bargained the fine process. The NFL’s officiating department reviews plays and refers potential fines to the football operations staff, which then examines the plays in question to determine whether a fine is in order. Players who get fined are sent a letter informing them of the fine and a video of the play in question. Players who don’t appeal have the money withheld from their next game check. Players who do appeal get a hearing with an appeals officer who is jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFL Players Association. This season, the appeals officers are Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson and James Thrash. The appeals officer has final say on whether or not the player gets fined.

Fine money is donated to the Professional Athletes Foundation, which supports former players in need, and the NFL Foundation, which supports health and safety initiatives in football from youth leagues to the professional level.

item.title: Seahawks pick different captains for each game, including Sam Darnold for Week 1
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When the Seahawks open the season on Wednesday night against the Patriots, quarterback Sam Darnold will be one of their captains.
item.content:encoded:
When the Seahawks open the season on Wednesday night against the Patriots, quarterback Sam Darnold will be one of their captains. But that won't be the case every week.

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald believes in picking new captains for each game, rather than the season-long captains with a 'C' on their jersey that most teams use. That was Macdonald's approach during his first two seasons as the Seahawks' head coach, and it will continue to be his approach this year.

In addition to Darnold, the Seahawks' captains against the Patriots will be linebacker Ernest Jones IV, fullback Brady Russell and defensive tackle Leonard Williams.

Macdonald said early in the 2024 season, his first as a head coach, that he believes in making team captain a weekly recognition rather than a season-long responsibility.

“It’s a combination of guys who are doing a great job, guys who are trying to build up and give an opportunity to have a voice with the rest of the team, guys you want to recognize that deserve an opportunity to do those things," Macdonald said. "So, that’s really the thought behind it. It’s pretty much that simple. The guys know who the leaders are. You don’t need the title to be the leader of the team. But it’s important to build everybody else up. . . . There’s nothing formal about it. It’s just more of a recognition type thing. Just, ‘Hey, shout out to these guys that are operating the right way, playing the right way, preparing the right way.’"

As the starting quarterback, Darnold was an obvious choice for Week 1. He'll be a team leader all year, and doesn't need the captain's 'C' to show it.

item.title: George Kittle "in good shape" to play season opener
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Tight end George Kittle traveled with the 49ers to Australia, which was a sign he would play in Thursday night's season opener.
item.content:encoded:
Tight end George Kittle traveled with the 49ers to Australia, which was a sign he would play in Thursday night's season opener. It sounds like Kittle will play, but how much remains to be seen.

"It's been pretty cool to see Kittle out there looking like himself, looking fresh," offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "How that affects him on game day and what the workload is, that will be determined. But he looks good to me.

"He's practicing full speed. He's getting a ton of reps. So I feel like we're in good shape."

Kittle tore his right Achilles in a Jan. 11 playoff game against the Eagles. He underwent surgery three days later, with Rams team physician Dr. Neal ElAttrache repairing Kittle's Achilles.

Kittle made his seventh career Pro Bowl last season despite playing only 11 regular-season games due to hamstring and ankle injuries. He recorded 57 receptions for 628 yards and seven touchdowns.

item.title: Raheem Morris confirms Nick Bosa will play season opener
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The 49ers defensive end tore his ACL in a Sept. 21 game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery Sept. 26.
item.content:encoded:
49ers defensive end Nick Bosa might need some time to get back to 100 percent, but he will play in the season opener.

Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris confirmed that Bosa's surgically repaired right knee is good enough to get him on the field against the Rams.

"Oh, he's going out there. Whatever you want to say, he's going. He'll be there. We're not hiding that," Morris said, via Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle.

Bosa, 28, said last week he thought he would be ready to go for Week 1, and he made the trip to Australia.

He tore his ACL in a Sept. 21 game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery Sept. 26. As he was coming back this summer, Bosa experienced soreness and tendinitis in his right knee, and the 49ers backed him down until Sept. 2 when he returned to practice.

Bosa has not had a double-digit sack season since 2023, which is the last time he played all 17 games. He has played only 17 games over the past two seasons, totaling 11 sacks.

item.title: Aaron Donald mum on plans for season opener
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan expects to see Aaron Donald on Thursday night, but like Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula earlier Monday, the defensive tackle declined to reveal his plans for the game in Australia.
item.content:encoded:
49ers coach Kyle Shanahan expects to see Aaron Donald on Thursday night, but like Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula earlier Monday, the defensive tackle declined to reveal his plans for the game in Australia.

The Rams are scheduled to leave for Melbourne on Tuesday night, and Donald wouldn't even commit to being on the flight.

“Taking it day by day. Come up with a game plan to see what's going on," Donald said, via video from Nick Hamilton of NBCLA. "Feeling good, feeling really good. Come up with a game plan and see.

"Honestly, man, I really do feel good. Things are clicking faster than I thought it would be. Even my first day out there, with 11-on-11, things would be a little all over the place. Settled in. A couple of plays a little rusty. It ain't where I want it to be, but it's pretty damn good if you ask me. To not play football in two years, to be moving how I'm moving, it's really no dropoff. It's not where I want to be. I can see it. I know there are things I want to clean up, that I'm going to clean up. The more reps I do, the more I play, it'll get there.”

Donald has started 11-on-11 drills in practice, but Monday was a planned recovery day. He worked on his cardio and did weight work instead.

"I'm 35," Donald said.

The three-time Defensive Player of the Year has not played in the NFL since 2023.

item.title: Report: Three teams have reached out to Darius Slayton
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Giants released wide receiver Darius Slayton on Monday, making him a free agent.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants released wide receiver Darius Slayton on Monday, making him a free agent. Slayton said in a social media post that he is "excited to see what’s next."

Josina Anderson of Exhibit News Network reports that three teams already have reached out to Slayton's representation for preliminary discussions. Anderson also mentioned the Colts as a potential destination, given Slayton's relationship with quarterback Daniel Jones.

Slayton spent seven seasons in New York, the longest tenured Giants player before his release. He was a fifth-round pick of the Giants in 2019, four rounds after the team drafted Jones.

Slayton and Jones played together six seasons.

Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards and one touchdown last season.

item.title: Derrick Henry: I am tired of watching the Super Bowl on TV
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Derrick Henry has played in one AFC Championship Game, a 35-24 loss to the Chiefs in the 2019 season.
item.content:encoded:
Derrick Henry has played in one AFC Championship Game, a 35-24 loss to the Chiefs in the 2019 season. After parting ways with the Titans, Henry signed with the Ravens because he believed he could win a title with Lamar Jackson at quarterback.

In Henry's two seasons in Baltimore, though, the Ravens have one playoff berth and one playoff win.

He still believes.

"It would be crazy for me to say I played with Lamar Jackson, and we didn’t win no championships," Henry said on "The Lounge" podcast, via Ryan Mink of the team website. "I cannot have that. I do not want that to be a thing. We've got to do it."

The Ravens lost to the Bills 27-25 in the divisional round in the 2024 playoffs and failed to make the postseason in 2025. The team fired coach John Harbaugh and hired Jesse Minter, and the Ravens revamped their defense in the offseason.

Henry said he "believes that we have all the pieces to get it done."

In nine postseason games, Henry has 211 touches for 1,090 yards and seven touchdowns. It hasn't been enough.

Jackson is 3-5 in his postseason career, with one trip to the AFC Championship Game.

"I want to win a Super Bowl. That's a big motivation," Henry said. "I just want to be able to feel that feeling. I'm tired of watching. Every year, I'm tired of being at home on the couch watching. I want to be a part of it. That's what's motivating me right now. I'm going to keep going until we get to that point. We have the 2026 season to get that accomplished."

item.title: Jacoby Brissett among Cardinals' team captains
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Jacoby Brissett who is in his first season as a starter for the Cardinals, was named one of five captains for the team this season.
item.content:encoded:
Jacoby Brissett who is in his first season as a starter for the Cardinals, was named one of five captains for the team this season.

On Monday, the Cardinals announced results of the players' captainship vote from Thursday.

Center Hjalte Froholdt was the other offensive captain. Safety Budda Baker and linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. were the defensive captains. Long snapper Casey Kreiter will represent the special teams.

"Whether you are a captain or not a captain, you be who you are within your own personality," coach Mike LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team website. "When you do get voted a captain, that says your teammates and the locker room looks up to you.

"I can't think of five better people to look up to, in terms of guys who will keep it real with each other, hold people to standards, communicate with me. I don't need to know everything that's going on in the locker room. I just need to know what's pertinent."

It is the fifth consecutive season for Baker to serve as a captain. Froholdt and Wilson are repeat picks, after becoming captains for the first time in their careers last year.

"There were quite a few guys who I won't mention who were right up there in the running for it," LaFleur said. "These guys are still going to have a voice, too. And some of it will be through the silent tape, if that makes sense. That's as important as anything, actually what you're doing [on the field]."

item.title: Darius Slayton: Grateful for time with Giants, excited to see what's next
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Wide receiver Darius Slayton's long run with the Giants came to an end on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Darius Slayton's long run with the Giants came to an end on Monday.

The Giants released Slayton less than a week before the start of the regular season and just over a week after there were rumors that he could be let go ahead of the cut to 53 players, so the move didn't come out of left field even though he was guaranteed $9.75 million this season. Having that money in the bank likely made it easier for Slayton to hear the news on Monday and his first response to it was filled with gratitude to the only NFL team he's played for.

"Grateful for my time in NY. 7 years a Giant nothing but love for one of the most prestigious organizations in the NFL. Excited to see what’s next," Slayton wrote on X.com.

The guaranteed money means that Slayton's next stop will likely be for a minimum salary and that should expand the pool of potential suitors for a player who led the Giants in receiving yards in four of his first five seasons.

item.title: Titans LB Cedric Gray injured in off-road vehicle accident
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Titans linebacker Cedric Gray has entered the NFL's concussion protocol after being injured in an off-field accident over the weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Titans linebacker Cedric Gray has entered the NFL's concussion protocol after being injured in an off-field accident over the weekend.

Gray was involved in a utility terrain vehicle accident over the weekend. A UTV, or utility task vehicle, is a rugged, off-road vehicle designed to carry passengers and haul heavy loads over rough terrain.

"Over the weekend, Cedric Gray was involved in a UTV accident in Tennessee and sustained a concussion and minor injuries," the Titans said in a statement. "We look forward to Cedric returning to the field soon and in full health when he clears the NFL's concussion protocol."

Gray started 16 games in 2026, and he ranked fifth in the NFL with a career-high 160 tackles.

A fourth-round pick in 2024, he played seven games with no starts as a rookie.

item.title: Rams DC Chris Shula: Everything's day by day with Aaron Donald
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Rams are moving closer to their trip to Australia for their season opener against the 49ers and it remains unclear if defensive tackle Aaron Donald is going to be on the field.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams are moving closer to their trip to Australia for their season opener against the 49ers and it remains unclear if defensive tackle Aaron Donald is going to be on the field.

Donald has been practicing with the team, but, per multiple reporters, defensive coordinator Chris Shula declined to say at a Monday press conference whether he's working in 11-on-11 drills at this point. Shula did say that the team is preparing for all possible scenarios as they put together their game plan for Thursday's game.

"Everything’s day by day," Shula said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times. "We’re ready for him if he does, ready for him if he doesn’t, and we’ll have a plan for however many plays he feels like he can go and we’ll go from there."

The 49ers expect to see Donald on the field in Melbourne and we'll find out in the next couple of days if that prediction is correct.

item.title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori remains limited, S Ty Okada DNP again on Monday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori remained limited in Monday's practice.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori remained limited in Monday's practice. That doesn't bode well for his availability for Wednesday's season opener against the Patriots.

Emmanwori did not take participate in any of the team’s open practices during camp, according to Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times. Emmanwori is working his way back from arthroscopic surgery in July to repair his right ankle, which he initially injured in the 2025 season opener and then aggravated in a practice before Super Bowl LX.

Starting safety Ty Okada's status for Week 1 also is in question as he missed a second consecutive day. The team's other starting safety, Julian Neal, was a full participant a second consecutive day with a quad injury.

D’Anthony Bell, who re-signed to the practice squad on Saturday, started two games in Emmanwori’s third safety role a year ago when Emmanwori was out with an ankle injury.

The Seahawks had only one change to their practice report from Sunday, with offensive guard Anthony Bradford (knee) upgraded to full participation. Bradford was limited on Sunday.

Wide receiver Tory Horton (hamstring) and offensive tackle Josh Jones (knee) again were limited.

Tight end A.J. Barner (oblique) and running back Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) remained full participants.

item.title: Mike LaFleur says he feels "good" about Jeremiyah Love's chances for Week 1
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle in an Aug. 13 preseason game against the Raiders.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle in an Aug. 13 preseason game against the Raiders. It was diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain, and he has not practiced or played since.

Love is moving closer to a return, though, and coach Mike LaFleur insinuated that the rookie did something on the practice field Monday.

"Progressing," LaFleur said, via Bo Brack of PHNX Cardinals. "He was out there moving around today. We'll see on Wednesday. I'll have a better idea for all those guys [who are injured]."

The Cardinals will have their first injury report of the season on Wednesday, which will be the first indication of where Love is in his rehab. LaFleur was asked about his optimism for the third overall pick to play against the Chargers.

"Yeah, I feel good," LaFleur said.

Love had 14 touches for 73 yards in the first half of the only preseason game he played.

item.title: Bill Belichick, to no surprise, has little to say about expanding UNC investigation
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Despite the team's 1-0 record, a storm has been blowing through the North Carolina football program, with most of it playing out privately.
item.content:encoded:
Despite the team's 1-0 record, a storm has been blowing through the North Carolina football program, with most of it playing out privately.

The situation became much more public last Thursday, with the abrupt resignation of G.M. Mike Lombardi followed by a report from WRAL indicating that the investigation that started with Lombardi has expanded to include defensive coordinator Steve Belichick and others.

Head coach Bill Belichick met with reporters on Monday, for the first time since the situation hit the fan. To no surprise, Belichick didn't have much to say in response to multiple questions about Lombardi, Steve Belichick, and the overall program.

The questions were posed despite an opening comment from a team spokesperson before Belichick took the podium, via WRAL: “Coach Belichick, student athletes, and other university employees will not discuss the situation in any manner. That is necessary to protect the integrity of the process and the rights of everyone involved.”

In his own introductory remarks, Bill Belichick mentioned “the importance of the work that's being done by the investigative team and, obviously, our high standard here of our code of conduct and doing things the right way and making sure that our student-athletes are given the utmost, the best treatment, the very best care, and the very best coaching that we can possibly give them."

He was then peppered with inquiries about the investigation, despite the effort to avoid talking about it.

The mere existence of an investigation that is exploring the behavior of multiple football employees shows that there's at least a question about whether the "high standard here of our code of conduct" has been met — including the question of whether the head coach knew about any of the potential irregularities and failed to report them.

Bill Belichick's potential failure to report issues of which he was aware becomes a potential recipe for a termination "for cause," which would cut off his buyout.

Frankly, the entire situation feels like an effort to find something that would give UNC an escape hatch from a hiring it already regrets, the upset win over TCU notwithstanding. And it creates an overriding vibe that his departure is inevitable. Possibly with no further financial obligation from the school to its second-year head coach.

item.title: Giants cut Darius Slayton
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The veteran wide receiver, who signed a three-year, $36 million contract last season, is out.
item.content:encoded:
Darius Slayton recently said he didn’t pay attention to rumors that he was at risk of getting cut. Apparently he should have.

The Giants announced today that they are releasing Slayton.

The move comes as a surprise if only because of Slayton's contract: Just last year, he signed a three-year, $36 million contract, and he is guaranteed $9.75 million this year. Cutting him only saves the Giants $2.5 million, but apparently they're down enough on him that they thought that savings was worth sending him packing.

The Giants presumably tried to trade Slayton before cutting him and found that no one wanted to trade for that contract.

Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards and one touchdown last season, and he's still good enough that some team will surely pick him up. Just not at anything close to what the Giants were paying him.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals didn't show concern about wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins missing Week 1 when they missed practice last week and the outlook continues to be good as they move closer to Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals didn't show concern about wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins missing Week 1 when they missed practice last week and the outlook continues to be good as they move closer to Week 1.

Chase and Higgins returned to practice on Monday. Chase hyperextended his knee in a practice and Higgins has been dealing with a heel contusion. Defensive end Shemar Stewart also practiced after returning to the field from a knee injury last week and head coach Zac Taylor made it sound like all three are on track to play.

"All three looked good today," Taylor said at his press conference. "We'll wait to release injury reports on Wednesday, but I was encouraged by the progress all three of those guys have made."

The Bengals would like to get off to a fast start this season and having all three players on the field against the Bucs would be a good step in that direction.

item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: It didn't take long for new Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin to establish himself as a team leader.
item.content:encoded:
It didn't take long for new Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin to establish himself as a team leader.

Franklin, who arrived in Green Bay via a trade in March, has been named one of the Packers' captains. That's not a surprise, as Franklin was a team captain on the Colts in each of the last six seasons. Some players exude leadership, and Franklin is one of them.

The Packers named five captains, Franklin and four players who were also Packers captains last year: quarterback Jordan Love, tight end Tucker Kraft, safety Xavier McKinney and special teamer Isaiah McDuffie.

Three players who were Packers team captains last year are not captains this year: Rashan Gary and Quay Walker, who are no longer in Green Bay, and Josh Jacobs, who is currently on the commissioner's exempt list amid an investigation into an accusation of violence against a woman.

item.title: Mike McCarthy hopeful that Joey Porter will play Week 1
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Steelers do not negotiate contract extensions once the season starts.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers do not negotiate contract extensions once the season starts. Thus, time is running out for the team to complete a long-term deal with cornerback Joey Porter.

"It’s a business, and there's definitely business conversations going on," head coach McCarthy said Monday, via Jack Markowski of SI.com.

McCarthy insinuated that he expects Porter to play regardless how talks turn out before Sunday's season opener against the Falcons.

"Yeah, I hope so," McCarthy said. "You know, just keep working him. He's still, I'd put him in a ramp-up mode."

When asked what happens if Porter doesn't play, McCarthy said, “We’ll see what happens.”

Porter practiced for the first time last Tuesday after spending all of training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list. But last week he was noncommittal about playing Week 1 absent a contract extension.

Porter, a second-round pick in 2023, is entering the final year of his rookie contract scheduled to make $3.924 million this year.

He is coming off a career year, totaling a career-high 14 passes defensed to go along with 52 tackles, one sack and one interception.

The Lions have filled one of the openings on their active roster.

They announced that they have signed linebacker Joe Bachie off of their practice squad. Bachie spent the offseason and preseason with the team and signed to the practice squad after failing to make the initial 53-man roster in Detroit.

Bachie opened last season with the Colts and started five games before landing on injured reserve. He moved on to the Titans after being released and played in 10 more games on special teams. He finished the year with 29 tackles and had 48 tackles in 51 games for the Bengals and Eagles earlier in his career.

The Lions still have one open spot on the 53-man roster after waiving center Seth McLaughlin and running back Jabari Small last week. They announced that both those players have been signed to the practice squad on Monday.

item.title: Bryce Underwood is Michigan's QB "right now," but his job security isn't "infinite"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood saved the Wolverines' bacon with a Hail Mary mulligan.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood saved the Wolverines' bacon with a Hail Mary mulligan. Underwood eventually may not be able to save his starting job.

“He’s our QB right now,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham told reporters on Monday, via Nick Kosko of On3.com. “And it’s not something that’s infinite. At some point, we’ve got to turn a corner and we’ve got to see improvement, as we do with a lot of stuff; you’ve got to see improvement out of the coaches, so it’s not just on Bryce. And it’s not just Bryce’s job that is not absolutely set in concrete. You’ve got to perform week in and week out and become somebody that is playing at a level we can win with.”

The program has made a significant financial commitment to Underwood, at $3 million per year. It's one of the realities of paying players; you need to pay the right ones.

Again, Underwood still has the job. Saturday night's performance against a MAC school was troubling, even with the late-game heroics. Underwood completed 12 of 22 passes for 170 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. He added 47 yards rushing and a touchdown, on nine attempts.

He'll need to perform at a higher level against better competition.

The next test happens on Saturday, when Oklahoma comes to town.

item.title: Steelers won't have full-season captains under Mike McCarthy
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's currently team captain season, with plenty of NFL franchises unveiling plenty of season-long captains.
item.content:encoded:
It's currently team captain season, with plenty of NFL franchises unveiling plenty of season-long captains. In Pittsburgh, however, there won't be a tweet with anywhere from five to 11 players listed as those who will be wearing a "C" in 2026.

New coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Monday that he won’t use full-season captains. Instead, he'll name captains for each week’s game. That's how McCarthy handled the captain designations while serving as the head coach of the Packers and the Cowboys.

The approach is a clear departure from past practices under Mike Tomlin, and another clear sign that some things will be very different with one Mike yielding to another.

Last year, the Steelers had four permanent captains: quarterback Aaron Rodgers, defensive lineman Cameron Heyward, linebacker T.J. Watt, and safety Miles Killebrew. (After Killebrew was lost for the season due to injury, linebacker Payton Wilson replaced Killebrew as the special-teams captain.)

item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys are going to be missing a starting offensive lineman for the first chunk of the regular season.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters at a Monday press conference that left guard Tyler Smith is going to have thumb surgery. Smith is expected to miss 4-6 weeks as a result of the operation.

item.title: Tua Tagovailoa's return to Pittsburgh puts extra pressure on Mike McCarthy's debut
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The last time quarterback Tua Tagovailoa started a game in Pittsburgh, it became his last start with the Miami Dolphins.
item.content:encoded:
The last time quarterback Tua Tagovailoa started a game in Pittsburgh, it became his last start with the Miami Dolphins. He was benched after the 28-15 loss on a Monday night in December — and he was cut in March.

Fast forward to September, and Tua will be returning to Pittsburgh as the Week 1 starter for the Falcons.

If it goes poorly, Tua may not be starting for very long. If it goes well, and if the Falcons upset the Steelers (Pittsburgh is currently favored by 3.5 points), there will be a very strong reaction in Western Pennsylvania.

Losing to Tua after drubbing him less than nine months earlier will provide the first clear apples-to-apples comparison between new coach Mike McCarthy and his predecessor, Mike Tomlin. Nuances will easily be lost on Steelers Nation. Yes, the Falcons are an overall better team than the 2025 Dolphins. The common denominator is the quarterback; if he plays dramatically better than he did the last time he played in Pittsburgh, Steelers fans will interpret that as an indication that the new boss won't have the same kind of success as the old boss.

It would be dubbed an overreaction. But that's what football fans do. With only seventeen games in a season, they all count. They all spark a reaction. And, at some point, the trend of overreacting shows that, actually, it's the normal and usual reaction to a team losing a game it should have won.

The Steelers have more than a few winnable games in the eight weeks before the bye, including two against the Browns. Anything less than 5-3 will spark high anxiety on and after Week 10, where the Eagles, Broncos, Texans, Jaguars, a road game at the Bengals, and two games against the Ravens are lurking.

The fans who show up in six days will be expecting a 1-0 start. If the end result is 0-1, sphincters will be tightening quickly in the Steel City.

item.title: Jovaughn Gwyn will start at center for Ravens in Week 1
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Ravens have named a starting center for their first game of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens have named a starting center for their first game of the 2026 season.

Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at a Monday press conference that Jovaughn Gwyn will be doing the snapping on offense against the Colts in Week 1.

It will be the first regular season start of Gwyn's career. He spent the last three seasons with the Falcons after entering the league as a 2023 seventh-round pick and moved on to the Ravens as a free agent this offseason.

Danny Pinter was seen as the leading candidate to land the starting job before he tore his patellar tendon. Veteran Ethan Pocic was the other option and Minter said that it is not a "permanent decision" to go with Gwyn in the middle of the offensive line.
